signals.signal: Cosmos core-banking programme has a hard finish date: the last deposit-account categories and customer profiles migrated on 26/05/2026 and the programme closed in early June 2026. Scale disclosed: >1,000 people across three continents, ~500,000 person-days, ~EUR 1bn invested in transformation over five years, phased from 2023 (corporate/SME loans) via consumer then mortgage loans to deposits by early 2026. NBG's COO is named as Stratos Molyviatis; Infosys Finacle with IBM and Deloitte; >6m customers, 12m deposit accounts, >1.5m loans migrated. Stated benefits: lower running cost, easier product parameterisation, cloud-readiness, easier integration of future acquisitions.
signals.source_name: PowerGame.gr (reporting NBG's 2Q26/1H26 analyst presentation) + Banking Technology magazine July/August 2026, p.04 (FinTech Futures news round-up, quoting NBG COO Stratos Molyviatis)
signals.implies: The core is done, so 2026-28 spend rotates to channels and infrastructure. Every self-service, ATM and POS driver now has to be re-certified against the new core - integration, testing and managed-services work Printec can bid, even though the core itself is closed to it (Infosys/IBM/Deloitte).
signals.likelihood: Certain (already executed); channel-integration follow-on work highly likely through 2026-27
signals.followup: Pull the 2Q26 presentation on 31/07/2026 and look for the first post-go-live IT cost/run-rate line and any 'channel modernisation' capex bucket.

signals.entity: National Bank of Greece (NBG) - international subsidiaries
signals.signal: Finacle adoption is expected to extend across ALL of NBG's international subsidiaries, 'a lot of which are long-standing users of Temenos' T24 core banking system'. NBG's international footprint is NBG Cyprus and Stopanska Banka AD Skopje (North Macedonia).
signals.source_name: Banking Technology magazine, July/August 2026 issue, p.04 (FinTech Futures news round-up; recovered from the publisher's own PDF after fintechfutures.com returned Cloudflare 403)
signals.implies: A multi-country core replacement pipeline. Core migrations force ATM/POS driver work, channel re-integration, reconciliation and test-automation - and in North Macedonia Printec is already the POS/acquiring incumbent in-market (Komercijalna), so Stopanska Banka is a warm approach. Cyprus is small but is Printec Cyprus's home patch.
signals.likelihood: Stated intent, no dates - decision/tender activity plausible within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Watch Stopanska Banka (stb.com.mk) and NBG Cyprus (nbg.com.cy) for core/channel programme announcements and NBRM disclosures; ask Printec North Macedonia whether Stopanska has opened a channel-integration workstream.

signals.signal: NBG Cyprus appointed Nicolas Prentzas as General Manager and Chief Operations Officer (announced 09/06/2026) - a technology/operations profile (BA Computer Science, Cambridge; career spent designing digital banking platforms, lending and payments products and automation), explicitly to serve 'digital transformation and customer service enhancement'. NBG Cyprus is corporate-focused: present since 1910, separate legal entity since 1994, two branches (Nicosia and Limassol), >140 staff.
signals.implies: No ATM fleet to sell into (two branches), so the fit is digital onboarding/eKYC, corporate channel/payments tooling and AML/compliance - plus he is the buyer for the Finacle rollout to Cyprus. A named ops/tech owner is the door.
signals.followup: Printec Cyprus to open a relationship with Prentzas; probe whether the Cyprus Finacle migration has a target date and who does the channel layer.

signals.signal: The post-core Technology & Processes workstream presented with 1H26 results is explicit: continuing modernisation of technology infrastructure via Appian workflows, CRM, and migration of the Enterprise Data Warehouse to cloud; new retail Mobile Banking platform; NEW Business Internet Banking; upgraded 'Next' app for the youth segment; GenAI rolled out bank-wide including the 'Sophia' chatbot. Retail service model adds in-branch relationship managers for high-potential clients plus remote RMs under 'Live Banking', marketed on nbg.gr as 'the full branch experience, 100% digitally'.
signals.source_name: PowerGame.gr (quoting NBG's own 1H26 presentation content) and nbg.gr ATM-network/digital-banking page
signals.implies: Branch role is being re-cut around advisory + remote video/RM service, which is the classic trigger for pushing cash to recyclers and assisted self-service. Live Banking and the in-branch RM model are branch-automation, queue/appointment and video-banking surfaces Printec sells without having to displace Mellon's Hyosung hardware.
signals.likelihood: In flight now; procurement decisions 6-12 months
signals.followup: Identify who supplies the Live Banking video/appointment layer and the in-branch customer-management front end; Appian is the workflow incumbent to integrate with, not fight.

signals.signal: NBG already markets a full business cash-automation line on its own site (checked 30/07/2026): cash deposit at ATMs using ETHNOdeposit deposit cards, cash deposit via 'Smart Safe' devices installed at the customer's own premises, and 'Instant Cash' deposit-to-account for professionals - all sold on immediate availability of funds in the business account. The same self-service/digital menu also lists Video Banking with online appointment, Online Nomimopoiisi (business/KYB legalisation) and onboarding for sole traders. No device vendor is named anywhere on the site.
signals.source_name: nbg.gr - Self-Service solutions for businesses / Cash deposits via Smart Safe / ETHNOdeposit pages
signals.implies: Direct hit on Printec cash automation/recyclers plus managed services: smart safes at merchant premises, CIT integration and provisional-credit reconciliation. Because the vendor is undisclosed, the incumbent is unknown and the estate size unpublished - the standing 'name the incumbent' task applies here.
signals.likelihood: Live product; expansion/refresh decisions plausible 6-12 months
signals.followup: Establish the Smart Safe OEM and installed base (ask Printec Greece sales; check Hellenic Business Registry filings of NBG cash-logistics suppliers); size the ETHNOdeposit-capable ATM subset now that NBG says deposit-capable ATM count was increased in 2025.

signals.signal: NBG Mobile Banking now carries Verification of Payee (VoP) - real-time check that the IBAN matches the named beneficiary before a transfer is completed - and Instant Payment Requests (IPR), both delivered under the EU Instant Payments Regulation; NBG maintains a dedicated 'SEPA Instant Payments - IPR Regulation' page for retail, professional and corporate segments.
signals.source_name: nbg.gr - Internet & Mobile Banking capabilities page
signals.implies: The IPR compliance layer is already built, so that door is largely closed. The residual pull is fraud screening on instant credit transfers and the same VoP/IPR obligations landing at the subsidiaries - and NBG builds its transaction monitoring in-house, so lead with HSM/security and payment-channel integration rather than monitoring.
signals.likelihood: Already delivered domestically; subsidiary rollout 6-12 months
signals.followup: Check whether Stopanska Banka and NBG Cyprus have VoP/IPR equivalents in flight (KIBS instant denar; Cyprus SEPA/TIPS).

signals.entity: National Bank of Greece (NBG) / Qivalis B.V.
signals.signal: NBG confirmed on its own press office that it has become a shareholder in Qivalis B.V. (Amsterdam), a consortium that expanded on 20/05/2026 to 37 European banks across 15 countries, seeking an Electronic Money Institution licence from De Nederlandsche Bank to issue a MiCA-compliant euro Electronic Money Token in 2H2026; reserves designed with at least 40% in bank deposits and the remainder in high-quality liquid bonds. Piraeus joined the same day.
signals.source_name: NBG Press Office (primary) and CaixaBank corporate news
signals.implies: A regulated stablecoin brings HSM/key management, wallet issuance and custody, wallet-holder eKYC and travel-rule/AML screening onto NBG's 2H26 roadmap - all Printec-adjacent (HSM/security, eKYC, AML). Consortium-level procurement may sit with Qivalis rather than NBG, so bid both.
signals.likelihood: EMI licence and launch targeted 2H2026 - decision-relevant inside 6 months
signals.followup: Track qivalis.eu press and the DNB register for the EMI authorisation; identify who supplies Qivalis's HSM/custody and KYC stack, and whether member banks run their own wallet onboarding.

signals.entity: National Bank of Greece (NBG) / Allianz SE
signals.signal: MoU signed 07/05/2026 for NBG to acquire a 30% minority equity stake in Allianz European Reliance (Allianz Greece), plus a long-term exclusive bancassurance agreement with an initial 10-year term and an automatic five-year extension. Allianz Greece is to provide a full general, health and life portfolio distributed through NBG's physical AND digital channels; subject to definitive agreements and regulatory approvals.
signals.source_name: Allianz SE media release; NBG press office media release PDF
signals.implies: A 10-year exclusive bancassurance build needs product onboarding, digital sales journeys, e-signature and identity verification across branch, app and web - eKYC/digital onboarding pull. It also validates NBG management's own argument that the new core makes acquisitions easy to absorb, i.e. more integration work ahead.
signals.likelihood: Definitive agreements and regulatory approvals expected over the next 6-12 months
signals.followup: Watch for the definitive agreement and the Hellenic Competition Commission / regulator filings; ask who builds the bancassurance digital journey.

signals.entity: Epirus Bank / NCR Atleos (Greek ATMaaS competition)
signals.signal: Epirus Bank selected NCR Atleos to modernise and expand its ATM network across Greece under Atleos's ATM-as-a-Service model with ATM Network Lifecycle Services - Atleos handles location selection, installation, maintenance and operational support - and uses the Cashzone network to create co-branded ATMs so the bank can cut operating cost and widen its footprint. Deployment started November 2025 with a phased rollout targeted for completion in roughly three months; announced 13/01/2026. This sits alongside DirectPay/iXchange on Cashzone (01/07/2025) and CrediaBank's move of its 141 ATMs to Euronet's ~2,500-machine network.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos press release (republished by The National Law Review)
signals.implies: The exact operator/carve-out trade Printec wants for NBG's 862 off-site ATMs is now being executed in Greece by two rivals (Atleos ATMaaS/Cashzone and Euronet). Cashflex's first-mover advantage from the Piraeus deal is eroding; Printec should take a costed ATMaaS proposition to NBG before the fee cap forces NBG's hand and a competitor gets the RFP.
signals.likelihood: High - Greek banks are actively outsourcing off-site estates under the ATM fee cap
signals.followup: Confirm Epirus Bank's unit count and whether an incumbent was displaced; benchmark Cashflex's economics against Atleos ATMaaS and Euronet before approaching NBG about its 862 off-site units.

signals.signal: In H1-2026 only ~330,000 IRIS transactions worth just over EUR 14m were made at physical points of sale, against 4.6m IRIS users, >600,000 enrolled professionals, ~1.2m POS terminals and 70,000 e-shops enabled - i.e. in-store account-to-account adoption remains marginal despite the December-2025 acceptance mandate. DIAS names the two unlocks as NFC tap-to-pay on mobile and loyalty schemes comparable to card rewards. IRIS connected to the EuroPA network in late June 2026 for phone-number transfers with Spain, Portugal and Italy, with EuroPA targeted to reach 18 European countries and ~176m users by end-2026 and e-commerce capability in 2027.
signals.implies: NFC-based IRIS at the POS means terminal software and certification work across the whole Greek acceptance estate, including NBG's i-Bank POS base - direct POS/acquiring work for Printec. EuroPA cross-border A2A adds scheme-integration and fraud/AML screening scope.
signals.likelihood: NFC IRIS at POS is a stated DIAS priority - specification/pilot activity likely within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Get DIAS's official H1-2026 statistics release (dias.com.gr) rather than press; ask NBG and Printec Greece whether IRIS-over-NFC terminal certification is scoped for the i-Bank POS estate.

signals.signal: Re-verified 30/07/2026: nbg.gr's own live corporate copy still advertises '356 branches and 1,476 ATMs', and the same 1,476 figure is still repeated in Greek press, while the audited 2025 Annual Financial Report (published 26/02/2026) gives 303 retail branches (48 tellerless) and 1,360 ATMs at 31/12/2025, split 498 on-site / 862 off-site (from 1,406 = 539/867 a year earlier). The in-branch hardware/software award of 16/01/2024 is also re-confirmed as 700 Hyosung Series-8 recyclers and cash dispensers with KAL K3A application and KTC management software, delivered by Mellon Technologies, and is explicitly scoped to IN-BRANCH operations only - it does not cover the off-site estate.
signals.source_name: NBG Annual Financial Report 2025 (Greek, primary PDF) and Mellon Technologies press release
signals.implies: Use 1,360 / 303, never 1,476 / 356. The 862 off-site units are outside Mellon's in-branch mandate, which is precisely why an off-site operator/ATMaaS carve-out is contestable for Printec rather than blocked by the Hyosung/KAL award.
signals.likelihood: Settled fact; next update with FY26 disclosures
signals.followup: Re-pull the 2Q26 presentation and the 1H26 interim financial report for the 30/06/2026 branch/ATM/tellerless counts and any change in the on-site/off-site split.
